title: The denominator df difference against ReplicateBE.jl is a boundary effect, and appears only at the boundary
raised_by: PR #62; closes the question PR #61 left open on EMA Data set I
effect_on_be_stats: none. The difference moves a 90% confidence limit by under 1e-4 percentage points, which is smaller than the rounding in every published figure this package is checked against.

the_open_question.observed: On EMA Data set I, be-stats gives a denominator df of 207.7350 and ReplicateBE.jl gives 208.0811 - a difference of 0.35, or 0.17%. Every other quantity agreed to six decimals.
the_open_question.leading_hypothesis: Data set I sits exactly on the correlation boundary (rho = 1.000), and the two implementations parameterise that limit differently. Unconfirmed, because one dataset cannot distinguish a boundary effect from a general one.

what_was_ruled_out_first.finite_difference_error: The Satterthwaite df needs the Hessian of the REML objective. An early version obtained it by second differences of the objective, which divides by h^2 and loses most of its significant figures. It was replaced with central differences of an ANALYTIC gradient with closed-form dV/dtheta. The df did not move, so the difference is not differencing error.
what_was_ruled_out_first.a_general_disagreement: Ruled out by the evidence below, which is what PR #61 could not obtain from one dataset.

the_evidence.design: Nine synthetic full-replicate cases, eight of them at interior optima and one constructed to land on the correlation boundary.

interior_cases.df_difference: below 1e-3 in every case; several agree to four decimal places at exactly n - 2
interior_cases.note: Cases B and D are excluded for an unrelated reason - see VAL-FDA-APPENDIX-C-003 - and are not counted either way.

comparison_with_data_set_i.reading: Same sign, same order of magnitude, same condition. The synthetic boundary case reproduces the real one.

the_evidence.conclusion: The difference appears at the boundary and only at the boundary. The hypothesis PR #61 recorded is confirmed.

mechanism.be_stats: G = LL' with theta = (l11, l21, l22, log s2_WT, log s2_WR). rho = 1 is l22 = 0, an ORDINARY INTERIOR POINT of R^5. The optimiser reaches it unaided - l22 = 2.7e-07 on Data set I - and no bound is applied. The REML Hessian is near-singular there, so satterthwaite_df uses a pseudo-inverse.
mechanism.replicatebe: CSH coordinates with the correlation behind a link. rho = 1 sends its parameter to infinity.
mechanism.reading: Two different delicate limits of the same quantity, approached from two directions. Neither is wrong; they disagree about the last three significant figures of a Hessian that is singular at the point in question.

why_the_tolerance_is_stated_in_df_and_no.reasoning: df matters only through the t quantile it selects, and the same absolute difference means very different things at 22 df and at 208.
why_the_tolerance_is_stated_in_df_and_no.data_set_i: t(0.95, 207.7350) = 1.652263 and t(0.95, 208.0811) = 1.652259 - a relative difference of 2.6e-6, moving the 90% interval by under 1e-4 percentage points.
why_the_tolerance_is_stated_in_df_and_no.the_test: asserts the CONSEQUENCE as well as the difference: the two t quantiles must agree to 1e-3 relative, which bounds the effect on a confidence limit at well under the 0.01 percentage points the comparison gate allows.

what_is_still_not_established.why_it_does_not_matter_here: EMA published Data set I's interval to two decimals, and both implementations reproduce it: 107.10 and 124.89 either way. The difference is four orders of magnitude below the published precision, so the published output cannot discriminate and does not need to.
what_is_still_not_established.what_would_settle_it: A SAS run reporting the df directly - the same shortest path VAL-FDA-APPENDIX-C-001 identifies for the partial replicate question.

consequence: Accepted and bounded. The boundary is not an edge case to be avoided: EMA Data set I - the only regulator-published Appendix C result available - sits on it, so an implementation that refused boundary solutions would refuse the one dataset that validates it.
